chunks: Abu Ḥabīb Nājiyah said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
I have a mill in which I grind sesame, and I rise and perform salat (prayer), while knowing that the servant-boy is asleep, so I strike the wall to wake him.
He عليه السلام said: “Yes, you are in obedience to your Lord, seeking your sustenance; there is no harm in that.”

key_terms.رَحًى: a millstone or mill used for grinding
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.ٱلسِّمْسِمَ: sesame seeds being ground for work and sustenance

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible during salat (prayer) to make a slight movement for the sake of work or livelihood?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that a small act during salat (prayer), such as striking the wall to wake a worker for necessary livelihood-related work, is not objectionable. The Imam عليه السلام affirms that seeking lawful sustenance while remaining in obedience to Allah is permissible and does not invalidate the act in this context.
